question: A storage box is in the shape of a right rectangular prism with internal dimensions 50 cm × 40 cm × 30 cm. How many liters can it hold?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of the rectangular prism = Length × Breadth × Height

⇒ Volume = 50 × 40 × 30 = 60000 cm³

Since 1000 cm³ = 1 liter, the capacity is calculated by dividing the volume by 1000.

⇒ Capacity = 60000 ÷ 1000 = 60 liters

**∴ The correct answer is 60 liters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (l) = 50 cm

Breadth (b) = 40 cm

Height (h) = 30 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a rectangular prism = l × b × h

1 liter = 1000 cm³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area is the sum of the areas of its six faces, given by the formula: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboidal box is its diagonal. Length of diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²).

Important Capacity Conversions

1 m³ = 1000 liters and 1 liter = 1000 cm³.
